title: clean:local deletes the JSON deployment artifacts but leaves addresses.ts / local-addresses.ts stale, so the in-repo consumer fails loudly while the external UI consumer fails silently
fingerprintProvenance: Copied VERBATIM from classified-findings.json, which copied it VERBATIM from sanitized-findings.json. Never recomputed, never retyped, never truncated — full 64 hex characters. Independently re-derived at write time from this record's own contract/function/rootCauseClass/entryPoint and confirmed to reproduce (see fingerprintVerifiedAtWrite).

description: `clean:local` is `rm -rf broadcast/*/31337 server/deployments/progress.31337.json server/deployments/local.json && rm -rf ~/.foundry/anvil/tmp/*`. It does NOT delete `server/deployments/addresses.ts` or `server/deployments/local-addresses.ts` — the two TypeScript artifacts the external UI repo actually imports. On any chain that aborts after the clean (and the clean runs first in both job 1 and again inside `deploy:local`), the workspace is left with NO JSON and STALE TypeScript. Demonstrated empirically: after running `clean:local` against a completed deployment, `progress.31337.json` and `local.json` were gone and `broadcast/DeployMocks.s.sol/31337` was removed, while `local-addresses.ts` was byte-identical (sha256 prefix c8e0355fbc73, unchanged) and still named `PhlimboV3: "0xC32609C91d6B6b51D48f2611308FEf121B02041f"`. The asymmetry is the finding, and it runs the wrong way round: the JSON consumers inside this repo fail LOUDLY and correctly — `server/index.js` re-reads both files on every request, so `/health` honestly flipped to `deploymentsLoaded:false` and `/contracts` returned HTTP 404 — but the TypeScript consumer, which is the external UI repo and therefore the entire point of stated purpose (b), has no staleness signal whatsoever. It simply imports addresses for contracts that no longer exist on any chain.
impact: A developer whose `npm run dev` aborted mid-chain, or who re-cleaned without redeploying, has a UI that builds and runs against addresses from a previous anvil session. On a fresh anvil those addresses are code-less; on a re-run they are frequently the same deterministic CREATE addresses for a DIFFERENT deployment generation, which is worse — the UI appears to work while reading a contract that is not the one it thinks it is. This is the concealment case the local-testing framing does not excuse.
attackPath: NONE. No attacker is involved in any of the five findings at this entry point; `dev` is an anvil-only script that is never broadcast. C4 requires an attack path only for High/Medium, and no finding here is graded above Low.
recommendation: Add `server/deployments/addresses.ts server/deployments/local-addresses.ts` to the `clean:local` rm list, so an aborted run leaves nothing rather than something stale. If the .ts files must survive for editor tooling, instead have `generate:ts-anvil` stamp a run id (block hash or timestamp) into both files and have the UI bootstrap assert it against `GET /health` — but deletion is simpler and fails in the safe direction.
recommendationProvenance: VERBATIM from sanitized-findings.json, byte-for-byte. Non-empty verified.

classification.c4Definition: QA/Low — incorrect state handling in a build/lifecycle script; a partial clean that leaves a stale artifact.
classification.assetImpact: None. `local-addresses.ts` / `addresses.ts` are generated from anvil state; `clean:local` does not touch the hand-maintained `mainnet-addresses.ts`. No mainnet contract, balance, or user is reachable from this defect.
classification.functionOrAvailabilityImpact: None to the protocol. Degrades the local dev loop: the external UI builds and runs against addresses from a dead deployment generation with no staleness signal.
impactChain: 1. `clean:local` rm's broadcast/*/31337, progress.31337.json and local.json but NOT addresses.ts / local-addresses.ts.
2. DEMONSTRATED (evidence/clean-local-stale-ts-demo.log): after a clean, both .ts files are byte-identical (sha256 prefix c8e0355fbc73) and still name PhlimboV3 at 0xC32609C9...
3. The in-repo JSON consumers fail LOUDLY and correctly - /health flips deploymentsLoaded:false, /contracts returns HTTP 404.
4. The external UI, which imports the .ts files, has NO staleness signal - the asymmetry runs the wrong way round.

5. On a fresh anvil the stale addresses are code-less (fails, if noisily); on a re-run, deterministic CREATE frequently reproduces the SAME address for a DIFFERENT deployment generation, so the UI reads a live-but-wrong contract and shows no error. This is the concealment case.
6. Realised harm: misattributed UI bugs and lost developer time, bounded to the local machine.
classification.likelihood: High as an occurrence (any aborted `npm run dev`, any re-clean without redeploy), low as a harm (surfaces the moment the developer exercises anything stateful).
classification.assumptions: Developer re-runs or aborts mid-chain without a full redeploy.
classification.attackPath: NONE. No attacker is involved in any of the five findings at this entry point; `dev` is an anvil-only script that is never broadcast. C4 requires an attack path only for High/Medium, and no finding here is graded above Low.
classification.localScriptRubric: KEEP - demonstrated concealment against the external UI consumer, which is the whole of stated purpose (b).
classification.lawNotes: Law 1: the concealment mechanism is the reason it is kept rather than filtered as a transparently-local shortcut.
classification.whyNotMedium: The silent-wrong-contract mechanism is the strongest Medium argument in the run and it is genuinely demonstrated, not hypothesised. It still falls short: the affected consumer is a local development UI on chain 31337, so nothing the protocol does becomes unavailable and no value can leak. A Medium here would rest on the same two-step 'a UI bug might therefore ship' conditional as DEV26-03, and the second step is undemonstrated. Low, ranked immediately below L-01.

rationale: A real, empirically demonstrated defect with a genuine silent-failure mechanism, but its entire blast radius is one developer's local session: the stale artifacts are the LOCAL address book on chain 31337, and no protocol asset or availability is touched.
